description: Per-case overrides applied on top of doc/spec/case_inventory.json for the Linux reference DUT (other DUT platforms supply their own overrides file via --inventory-overrides). Four independent axes: (1) `expected:false` (+ `reason`) marks a spec case the harness intentionally cannot cover (e.g. wall-time-permanent-deferred shapes) — counted as a gap by `--vs-spec`; (2) `platform_known_fail:true` (+ `platform_known_fail_ref`) marks a case that fails on this file's target platform due to platform-specific kernel/stack deviations from RFC MUST/SHOULD but passes on a strict-RFC DUT — kept ACTIVE in coverage reports so spec coverage stays honest, and filtered out of CI/smoke skip lists via `--exclude-platform-known-fail`; (3) `timing_serial:true` (+ `timing_serial_ref`) marks a case whose verdict measures a sub-second inter-frame cadence (a strict frame_delta_within_us window) that the reference DUT can only meet when NOT CPU-starved — CI runs these UNCONTENDED (--workers 1) via `--only-serial` and drops them from the parallel lane via `--exclude-serial`, mirroring how a conformance lab measures timing on dedicated DUT hardware; the case stays ACTIVE in coverage. (4) `requires_secondary_iface:true` marks a case the smoke harness must execute with a second tester interface (TC8 Topology 2 dual-broadcast-domain, e.g. USAGE_01) — surfaced via `--only-secondary-iface` so the harness brings up the second veth + passes `--interface-secondary` data-drivenly rather than by hardcoded case-ID. It is a harness-wiring need, NOT the overloaded spec `kTopology` number (UDP 'Topology 2' is two source hosts on ONE iface). The axes are disjoint in practice but can coexist on a single entry. Schema v3 renamed the second axis from `linux_known_fail` when the lwIP DUT became the second platform consumer; v4 added the third (timing_serial) axis; v5 added the fourth (requires_secondary_iface) axis. (A `_NEG` self-validation case's per-DUT applicability is NOT an inventory axis: it is derived from the DUT's own OpQueryCapabilities (0x16) bitmap via the case's `kRequiredCapabilities` + the Tier-2 capability-skip gate — the DUT is the SSOT for what it can fault.)
